Consult Summary:
- Young female with 2 days of central lower abdominal pain, associated mild nausea, subjective feverishness/sweating and a reported slight pink discoloration of urine; clinician suspected a urinary tract infection and arranged a short course of oral antibiotics with safety-netting.

History:
- Presenting complaint:
  - Central lower abdominal ("lower tummy") pain for 2 days.
  - Feels hot and sweaty; patient reports feeling shivery/sweaty at times.
  - Mild nausea without vomiting.
  - Noted slight pink discoloration of urine (described as "a little bit pink").
  - Increased urinary frequency a little; no pain on passing urine.
- Timeline:
  - Pain onset: 2 days prior to consultation.
  - Constipation noted during the prior week but resolved; last bowel movement ~2 hours before consult and was normal.
  - Measured temperature ~37.0°C about one hour before consult.
- Exacerbating/relieving/initiating factors:
  - None specifically reported.
- Associated symptoms / review of systems:
  - No vomiting.
  - No back pain.
  - No vaginal discharge.
  - Regular menstrual periods; no intermenstrual or postcoital bleeding.
  - No recent travel.
- Pertinent negatives:
  - No prior similar problems.
  - No dysuria.
  - No significant past medical problems reported.

Past Medical History:
- No chronic medical conditions reported.
- No prior similar episodes.
- Family history: mother had breast cancer, treated/cured (patient reports).

Medications:
- Patient reports no regular medications.
- Contraception: patient stated she "had the internal contraceptive implant for one year, now no more" — conflict noted regarding current status; dose/route/frequency not documented.
- Over-the-counter: none reported.

Allergies:
- Amoxicillin allergy reported.

Social History:
- Lives with parents.
- Smoking: denies tobacco smoking.
- Alcohol: drinks approximately 4 times per week, about one beer per occasion.
- No other substance use reported.
- No financial or other lifestyle factors reported.

Family History:
- Mother: breast cancer, treated and reportedly cured.

Physical Examination:
- No physical examination findings documented.
- Vitals: patient-reported temperature ~37.0°C (measured at home); no other vitals documented.

Investigations:
- No investigations performed or results available/documented in the transcript.

Assessment & Plan:
- Issue 1: Suspected urinary tract infection (clinical impression by clinician)
  - Assessment: Lower central abdominal pain, mild urinary frequency, reported pink urine, subjective feverishness — clinician suspects urinary tract infection.
  - Plan:
    - Offer of a short course of oral antibiotics discussed; patient consented to receive antibiotics via allocated pharmacy.
    - Antibiotic course described as twice daily for 3 days (antibiotic name/dose/route not documented).
    - Patient advised to start antibiotics as soon as received.
    - Safety-netting: return/contact if pain worsens, develops high temperature, back pain, new symptoms, or if not improving — may require face-to-face assessment for examination.
    - Advice to contact service if recurrence of same problem.
- Issue 2: Reported hematuria (pink urine)
  - Assessment: Small amount of pink discoloration reported by patient; source not confirmed.
  - Plan:
    - Monitor while on treatment; further investigation not documented in transcript.
- General Plan items:
  - Prescription to be sent to patient's allocated pharmacy (patient confirmed pharmacy registered with service).
  - No additional tests or referrals documented.

Quality checks:
- Missing but clinically expected elements:
  - No clinician-performed physical examination documented.
  - No vital signs recorded other than patient self-measured temperature (~37.0°C).
  - No point-of-care urine dipstick/urinalysis or urine culture results recorded.
  - No pregnancy test documented (relevant for a woman of reproductive age, contraceptive implant status unclear).
  - Antibiotic name, exact dose, and route not documented.
  - Clarification needed regarding current status of contraceptive implant.
- Internal conflicts from transcript:
  - Contraceptive implant: patient stated she "had" it for one year and also said "no more" — conflict noted regarding whether implant is currently in place.
- Transcript quality:
  - Generally understandable; occasional brief inaudible/overlapping segments but sufficient to extract clinical history and plan.
